description:
Moves command dispatch out of the 6,400-line `run()` in `crates/jit/src/main.rs` into library-side handlers that return typed command or domain results and failures as values, on top of one global `--json` flag and one shared issue-filter argument group.

## Background

`run()` matches over the 29 `Commands` variants and builds success payloads, chooses error codes, prints and calls `std::process::exit` inside the arms. `cli.rs` declares 108 per-command `json` fields, `main.rs` scans raw argv for `--json` twice, 13 hidden verb stubs shadow the parser-level hint path, issue filters are parsed at about 14 sites, and 74 of 120 schema leaves fall back to `CommandResponse`. Several arms reach `storage`, `jit::search`, the claims free functions and the serve process helpers directly instead of the executor or `commands/`.

On main, `run()` in `crates/jit/src/main.rs` parses the arguments and calls `dispatch()` in `main.rs`, which holds the command match; the arms and inline code this issue places in `run()` live in `dispatch()`.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: `--json` is one global flag carried as `OutputMode`; no subcommand declares a `json` field, no code reads raw argv for it.
- [hard] REQ-02: No hidden verb-hint stub remains; a wrong verb prints its hint and clap's diagnostic on stderr and exits 2, with or without `--json`.
- [hard] REQ-03: Every issue-filtering command takes its filters from one flattened `IssueFilterArgs` group parsed once at the CLI boundary.
- [hard] REQ-04: Every command group dispatches from `run()` to a handler in `crates/jit/src/dispatch/`, and every visible schema leaf names the typed command or domain result its handler returns.
- [hard] REQ-05: Handlers return failures and findings as values: no handler substitutes a fallback code for an ordinary error, prints an error envelope or calls `std::process::exit`; declared findings use the shared outcome/emitter, and worktree execution retains child-status passthrough (exit 1 when no numeric status exists), while foreground serve remains a typed failure, and each deliberate exit-code, envelope or schema change has a test stating the new contract.
- [hard] REQ-06: The migrated handlers make no storage, `jit::search`, claims free-function or serve process call; they go through the executor or `commands/`.

## Notes

Design rationale: `dev/active/df129d9e-rust-code-quality/plan.md`; inventories with function and arm citations: `dev/active/df129d9e-rust-code-quality/investigation.md`.
## Decisions

- D-01: Reconcile response ownership with the user-approved epic REQ-01 and plan D-59: command or domain results are rendered and enveloped by output, without a command-to-output dependency.

- D-02: Reconcile REQ-05 with the accepted findings protocol (plan D-42) and the 0eca332a D-02 boundary correction. The steward approved the existing findings and worktree child-status behavior on 2026-11-04; ordinary errors still require canonical typed classification, with no new arbitrary-code sites or behavior change.
title: Library-side command dispatch for crates/jit
